title: Surface area to volume ratio falls as a cell grows
caption: For a cube of side L the surface area is 6L² and the volume L³, so the ratio is 6/L: doubling the side halves it. A 2 µm cube has 3 µm² of surface for every µm³ of volume; a 4 µm cube only 1.5.
alt: A curve of surface area to volume ratio against the side of a cube, falling steeply from 12 at 0.5 micrometres to 1 at 6 micrometres, with points marked at 1, 2 and 4 micrometres.
description: The ratio is surface area ÷ volume = 6L² ÷ L³ = 6/L.
A 1 µm cube: 6 µm² ÷ 1 µm³ = 6 per µm.
A 2 µm cube: 24 µm² ÷ 8 µm³ = 3 per µm.
A 4 µm cube: 96 µm² ÷ 64 µm³ = 1.5 per µm.
Each doubling of size halves the surface available to supply each unit of volume.
axisLabels: side of the cube, L / µm
